rationale:
I SHOT THE TOWN BEFORE PLANNING IT — seed 42, four instants (day 5 07:45 early summer, day 65 12:58 autumn clear, day 6 dusk, and the lane and courtyard crops at noon) — and one band decides this batch. The ROADWAY. LN_ROAD0 68..76 is eight rows across all 138 columns, ~9% of the world, the single longest continuous line in every framing and the thing a viewer's eye slides down to after the courtyard. It is built with more care than almost anything in the town: settGrid/settRun, camberZ, gutterF, rutF, KERB_RUN, paveWear, PUDDLES. On a clear autumn midday with 73 people out, the lane crop shows exactly TWO things on it — one cyclist and one figure. Then I greped rather than trusted the picture, and the cause is structural, not a rate: LANE_N_Y 66.4 and LANE_S_Y 77.3, the two walking lines, both sit on the FOOTWAYS; every one of spawnLaneAgent's branches picks one of them; and the only object in 210 iterations that has ever driven on the carriageway is `cart`, one dray, on market days, at CART_LANE_Y. The town built a road and then walked around it. That is fabric, not an event — the managerWatch note's own test — and it changes the wide shot in the first ten seconds, which is what a bet is for.

RUNG 2, AND I AM SAYING SO RATHER THAN DRESSING IT UP. This batch deepens and interconnects systems that already exist; nothing here widens the menu, moves the census, or changes the observer. The last five passes were 4b/5/4a/3/5, so one low pass is legal and this is the first of at most two — the pass after next climbs to 3+ whatever it finds, and the named claim on it is the Interaction column (15 of 210, 8 of them sill chrome; four domains have never had one).

TWO PREMISES DIED BEFORE THEY BECAME BRIEFS, WHICH IS THE POINT OF SHOOTING FIRST. (1) 'Nothing in this town casts a shadow' — the midday and morning wides both look shadowless, and it is false: buildSunShade()/shTop/shCast/shOpen throw every solid volume from sunVec(), at BSH_MAX*daylight*shadowF(), which is faintest at dawn and shortest at noon by construction. Filed as a worker WATCH note so the next pass to see that picture does not write the brief I nearly did. (2) 'The near roof reads as one flat texture' — dead three times already (c232/c259/c271, sd/mean 0.281, the highest large surface on the record); I did not write it a fourth time.

THE OTHER FOUR ARE THE LONGEST-NEGLECTED DOMAINS, EACH CARRYING A NUMBER. b212 courtyard (12 back): buildMossRegion is called exactly twice, for PLAZA and QUAY, and the piece's namesake — the largest paved surface in the town — is the one big paving that does not age with the year. b213 roofs (11 back): grep finds no drip, downpipe, gutter or runoff anywhere in 1.25 MB of source; the roofs wet (drawSlateCell mixes on wetF) and shed nothing, and the lane already has PUDDLES/pudHollow waiting for a foot to form under. b214 nearblock (9 back) and b215 life (8 back) spend c298 and c299, both of which arrive with their probe and their number already measured.

WHAT I CUT, AND WHICH WAY EVERY CAP MOVED. No cap was raised; two things were cut to fit under caps that did not move. INVENTORY 11.7 -> 9.8 KB against an unchanged 10.0: the market's day was re-filed from `street` (where #207 had put it) into the lane line that owns it, #209's weed-steering merged into the weeds CA line, sill's 9 entries merged to 6, and every remaining line stripped of tuning constants and coordinates — which is what the file's own note has always said belongs in the source. Two entries deleted outright: sill's HARNESS line (instrument nouns; SKILL.md names every gate already) and sky's two-PRNG-streams line (that is a LAW, and LAWS.md carries it). LAWS.md 25 -> 26 laws at 11.9/12 KB: added #206's (a frame's share is a function of the ZOOM alone), #207's control-saturation clause and its two ink-measurement liars with #208's, and merged #209's and #210's into the laws they extend — paid for by SUPERSEDING the two-layouts law, whose claim that 'the wide view is resize()'s raw cellW/topPad' #206 made false; by deleting the CAST/MIRROR clause of trap (a) (buildSunShade/shOpen and drawWaterMirror carry it in the source, and the new watch note points at them by name), the residual FALL-THROUGH clause, the short-run RAMP clause (subsumed by 'pool six seeds and a YEAR'), a route-cost restatement and a TIMEOUT clause; and by SPLITTING the ground-cache law, 902 B against the 900 B advisory, into its two claims. Cues 8 -> 6: two promoted (c298 -> b214, c299 -> b215), c305 closed on its own probe's evidence, c308 raised. Worker read 45.6 -> 44.0/46 KB, every sub-cap met.

queue.brief: THE BET, AND IT IS MEANT TO BE BIG — 150-300 lines are expected and welcome. The town has a road and nothing drives on it. `LN_ROAD0 68..76` is eight rows x 138 columns of laid setts with camber, gutters, ruts and kerbs, it crosses the whole width of every framing, and in 210 iterations the only object that has ever travelled it is the single `cart`/dray on market days. Both of spawnLaneAgent's walking lines (LANE_N_Y 66.4, LANE_S_Y 77.3) are on the FOOTWAYS. Give the carriageway continuous traffic: a stream of vehicles that enters at one end and leaves at the other, sized by the hour, the day and the weather the lane already knows. FABRIC, not an event — something is on the road in most frames, not a thing that happens at 11 o'clock. Price it before you build it: count what is on the roadway per sample over six seeds x a year on HEAD, so 'the road is empty' is a number and not my screenshot. Then size the population the way LAWS.md says — a ~40 s crossing at CART_SPEED-ish is a resident, so floor the arrival RATE and let trip length set how many are in frame. Re-use before you invent: `cart`'s heading ease, `cartShove()`'s berth and the walker-dodge it already implements are the precedent for anything on wheels, and the roadway is already in the ground cache, so a moving vehicle is a LIVE overlay and must not dirty it.
queue.successLooksLike: In the wide shot at a busy hour something is moving along the carriageway in most frames, and the lane crop at 1600x950 shows traffic where it now shows one cyclist. On a wet day or after dark there is measurably less of it, off the weather scalars the lane already reads. Quote roadway occupancy per sample, HEAD vs candidate, over six seeds x a year, and the diff image's mass as a ratio to a same-code control.
queue.avoid: Do not add another walker band — eastEdges already has six and the cyclist and the dog have fixed widths for a reason (see the comment above EAST_TAIL). Do not put anything on the roadway that stops there: this is TRANSIT, and a parked thing is roof furniture. Do not touch the market, the cafe or the kiosk. Do not widen or re-lay the road surface; it is right, it is simply unused. Anything drawn per frame must be a live overlay — do not set groundDirty from it.

queue.brief: The piece's namesake is the one big paving that does not age. `buildMossRegion()` is called exactly twice — MOSS_PLAZA over the plaza's PATH, MOSS_QUAY over the quay's SIDE — and the courtyard's own flags, the largest paved surface in the town and the brightest thing in every wide shot, were left out. The machinery is already general: mossOwn[] masks the region, the creep stops at a change of owner, mossShel/mossTop set the ceiling per cell, MOSS_BUCKET quantizes the draw, MOSS_SCUFF wears it under feet, and trodStone() puts it in groundBase. Give the courtyard the third region. Its regime is genuinely different from the other two and that is the point: it is WALLED, so shelter is high; it has EDGE_BEDS on all four ranges and now an ARCADE along the north, so the damp edges are where moss should gather; and its ring path carries the densest foot traffic in the town plus a pre-dawn sweeper, so the desire lines should read as CLEAN stone through a green that thickens at the walls and under the arcade. Price the premise first: how much moss the plaza actually shows through a year on HEAD, and whether the courtyard's own shelter and scuff leave anything standing — if the answer is that the ring scours it flat, the measurement is the deliverable and say so.
queue.successLooksLike: Through an autumn and a winter the courtyard's flags green at the walls and under the arcade while the ring path stays stone, and the plaza and quay regions are BYTE-IDENTICAL to HEAD (mossOwn is a mask; a new owner must not leak into either). Census PASS, and quote the courtyard's mean moss by season against the plaza's.
queue.avoid: Do not re-tune MOSS_GROW/MOSS_DIE/MOSS_COLD/MOSS_DRY — they are the plaza's and the quay's, and moving them moves two shipped systems. Do not add a second wear array: paveWear[] and wear[] already exist and MOSS_SCUFF is the scuff term. The lawn is GRASS, not paving; the region stops at the flags.

queue.brief: It rains on this town and the water never leaves the roofs. A grep of the whole source finds no gutter, no downpipe, no eave drip and no runoff anywhere: the roofs are the top third of every wide frame and the largest sloped surface in the picture, they DARKEN when wet (drawSlateCell and drawRoofRow both mix on wetF), and nothing carries a drop off them. Give the houses their rainwater goods — a gutter line along the eave and a downpipe down the face, placed off the geometry that already exists rather than a new list, and let them do something: on a wet day the eaves drip and the pipes run; on a dry day the town gains a vertical rhythm on a hundred facades that it has never had. Then CONNECT it, which is the half that makes this worth an iteration: PUDDLES[] and pudHollow[] already stand water on the pavement off the GRID, and the foot of a downpipe is where a puddle belongs — bias the hollow there rather than adding a new puddle source. Read the traps first: roofs are EMERGENT from buildVolumes(), so read eaveFor()/roofZE() and change no footprint; a FACE is drawn only where the SOUTH neighbour is open, so a pipe on any other side will never be seen; and both the facades and the ground are CACHED, so a static pipe registers at cache time while a running one is a live overlay.
queue.successLooksLike: At the shipping size, on a dry day the facades read with a regular vertical accent they did not have; in rain the eaves are visibly running, and the pavement under a pipe holds water sooner than the pavement beside it. Quote the wet-day diff's mass as a ratio to a same-code control, quote it at the SHIPPING size, and show the dry-day frame is not cluttered.
queue.avoid: Do not change a footprint or a roof height — the roofs are emergent and the law is explicit. Do not add a per-drop particle system; this is fabric, and the rain already has stepDrops(). Do not create a second puddle source: bias pudHollow, do not bypass it. Do not put pipes on the near block's slates without checking nearScale — at NEAR_SZ 1.95 anything drawn there is twice the size it is across the lane.

queue.brief: c298: `freeBay()` starves its index-0 bay. On HEAD, over six seeds x a year, house 1 took 0.35-0.75% of daylight samples to house 7's 4.9% — a 7x gap on a terrace whose whole promise is that it is somebody's (probes/terrace-presence.mjs measured it and is on disk). #201's filter evened it by accident and the branch was never examined, so nobody knows whether the bias is in freeBay(k,want)'s scan order, in leadsKit(bay)'s furnishing, or in spawnTenant's choice of house. Find which, fix it at the one place it lives, and re-run the probe. This is the domain's SECOND iteration ever and its whole surface is 20% of the wide frame and ~34% of the phone's, so a tenant who is only ever on one end of it is a visible fault, not a statistical one.
queue.successLooksLike: probes/terrace-presence.mjs over the same six seeds x a year shows the per-house daylight-presence spread inside a factor of ~2 rather than 7x, with the total presence unchanged — this is a redistribution, not more tenants. Census byte-identical to HEAD if no behaviour but the choice moved.
queue.avoid: Do not raise TEN_CAP or TEN_STAND to paper over it — the cap is not the fault and a raised cap hides the diagnosis. If the measurement says the gap is by construction and correct, say so and close the cue: a killed premise is a good iteration.

queue.brief: c299: the martins' second mud source is the same in every world. #202 gave the colony a strand — `martStrandF()` off the river's drying bank — but the strand is built from `hash()`, which is NOT seeded, so a rainless colony now founds on the SAME days in every seed and the worlds differ only in which birds turn up. LAWS.md states the rule this breaks: hash() is one town in every world, and a per-day hash is one sample of the calendar in every seed — SALT it when the calendar must differ per world. Put a per-world salt on the level's lag so the mud year runs on a per-town clock, the way the cart's calendar (WIND_SALT) and the fair's (isFairDay) already do. Price it as the laws require: histogram the founding day over the YEAR across six seeds on HEAD and on the candidate, and show the distribution is the same SHAPE with the seeds no longer in lockstep — this is a fidelity fix, not a behaviour change, and the colony's size and timing must not move.
queue.successLooksLike: Founding day across six seeds spreads instead of coinciding, while the per-seed distribution over a year keeps HEAD's shape and the colony's mean size is inside the seed noise. Name the salt in the source next to the two that precede it.
queue.avoid: Do not spend an R() draw on this — the strand is hashed and must stay hashed, or every downstream draw in the world reshuffles (LAWS.md: any new draw reshuffles the whole seeded world). Do not touch MART_WET or the rain source; only the strand's clock is at issue.
